title: Americans Use Less Cash, but Still Carry It
paragraphs: Many Americans do not use cash very much anymore. But a lot of them still carry it, a new study says.
The study was done by Pew Research Center, a research group in the US. It asked 9,750 adults in the US about cash in May and June 2026.

The study found that 42% of Americans do not use cash for any purchases in a normal week. In 2015, this number was only 24%. So, many more people now pay with cards or phones. Only 12% of people said they use cash for all or almost all of their purchases.

But many people still keep cash with them. About 46% of Americans said they carry cash always or most of the time. About one in five said they carry cash sometimes, and 32% said they rarely or never carry it.
Interestingly, carrying cash is not the same as using it. About 26% of people who usually carry cash said they do not use it to buy anything in a normal week.

Income also makes a difference. Half of people in homes that make $100,000 or more a year usually carry cash. But people with less money use cash more for shopping. About a quarter of people who make less than $30,000 a year use cash for all or almost all purchases.
Age is important too. Young adults are much less likely to carry cash than older people.
So, cash is not gone yet. But it is becoming less important in the lives of many Americans.
